parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/user/user.entity.ts sits in the domain layer because of the **/*.entity.ts pattern, but it does more than model the user. It is a TypeORM persistence mapping, which belongs in infrastructure. The class is a table mapping (@Entity('user')). Every field carries a column decorator (@PrimaryGeneratedColumn, @Column). Relations are defined with join-table details (@ManyToMany plus @JoinTable, and @OneToMany). On top of that, the method hashPassword() hooks into the ORM's insert lifecycle through @BeforeInsert and uses argon2 to hash the password. Hashing during a persistence lifecycle event is infrastructure work (persistence and crypto), not domain behaviour. The domain class therefore depends on the ORM's lifecycle. The class-validator @IsEmail decorator is input-validation framework logic, which usually belongs in application DTOs or presentation, although this point is weaker. The rubric gives "persistence ... or framework logic in a domain file" as an example of a fail, so this file fails.

violations.message: The domain-layer class UserEntity is a TypeORM persistence mapping (@Entity('user'), @PrimaryGeneratedColumn, @Column, @ManyToMany/@JoinTable, @OneToMany). Table and column mapping is an infrastructure (persistence) responsibility.

The hashPassword() method, triggered by @BeforeInsert, hashes the password with argon2 inside an ORM insert lifecycle hook. Hashing at persistence time is infrastructure work and makes the domain class depend on the ORM's lifecycle.
The @IsEmail() decorator from class-validator on the email field adds framework input-validation logic to a domain file. This belongs in application DTOs or presentation validation.
